                                                                              PM FIRE WEATHER FORECAST
                                                                                            ISSUED: 1100 Friday October 09 2026


Today: A deep surface low over SW Alberta and its associated warm front will bring 20-40mm, locally 50mm, of rain/wet
snow to the southern boreal and Rockies. The cold front will move from JP to BO in the afternoon, bringing 5mm of rain/wet
snow with a slight risk of TRW in the region. Highs 2-10°C in the boreal to ED, 11-15°C south to Red Deer, and 17-23°C in
the far south. RH values remain above 60%, except 25-30% south of RM. N-NE winds 30-40km/h with gusts to 55-65km/h
in the boreal, and SW winds 35-40km/h with gusts to 70-80km/h in southern Alberta.

Tomorrow: The low will depart into SK by morning, but lingering precipitation and upslope flow will bring an additional 5-
8mm of wet snow to the east slopes and southern boreal/northern AG. A ridge will build in the north, bringing settled weather
north of Slave Lake. Highs 0-8°C across the province, except -4 to 0°C in the Parks and SW boreal. RH values remain above
55%. Winds N-NE20-30km/h with gusts up to 50km/h in the SE boreal/AG/east slopes. Elsewhere, N10-15km/h.

Outlook for Sunday: An upper ridge will settle over northern AB, bringing clearing skies, except for light wet snow in
CR/WP/southern AG from a trough extending north from the US. Max temps -1 to +5°C with RH above 55%, except 35-45%
in the NW boreal. Winds S15-25G45km/h in the boreal and NE10-15km/h elsewhere.

Outlook for Monday: An upper ridge building in from BC and a surface ridge extending from Hudson Bay to southern AB
will maintain stable weather. An upper trough deepening along the Pacific coast will bring a change in weather by midweek.
Max temps 6-10°C with min RH 25-30% along the eastern slopes and 45-60% elsewhere. Winds SW15-20G35-40km/h in
the boreal/AG and SW10km/h elsewhere.
